Estimate the USD cost of a set of calls

Source: R/core-transport-models.R
hr_estimate_cost.Rd

Estimate the USD cost of a set of calls

Usage

hr_estimate_cost(
  model,
  input_tokens,
  output_tokens = 0,
  cached_input_tokens = 0,
  detail = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

Model id.

input_tokens, output_tokens

Token counts (scalars or vectors; vectors are summed).

cached_input_tokens

How many of input_tokens the provider served from its prompt cache. They are priced at the model's cached_input_usd when it has one, and as other input tokens when it does not.

detail

FALSE (the default) for the figure alone; TRUE for a data frame that also says where the prices came from.

Value

A single numeric USD figure, or NA_real_ when the model has no pricing in the registry, or no output price and output_tokens above zero (an embedding model's missing output price counts as zero, since it produces no output tokens). harnessr ships no prices: set them with hr_register_model() or hr_load_models(). Treat the figure as an estimate. When the model's prices are older than hr_options("price_max_age_days") (120 days by default, counted from the first day of their as_of month), the first figure computed from them in a session warns with class hr_stale_price.

With detail = TRUE, a one-row data frame instead: model, usd (the same figure), priced (whether the model has a price), as_of (the month of its prices, NA without one) and certain (FALSE when the model's registry entry is a family guess or the default; see hr_model_info()).

See also

hr_model_info(), hr_register_model(), hr_trace_summary()

Other cost and token functions: hr_budget(), hr_context_fit(), hr_context_policy(), hr_count_tokens(), hr_load_models(), hr_model_info(), hr_model_limits(), hr_models(), hr_register_model(), hr_set_tokenizer(), hr_tokenizer(), hr_truncate(), hr_truncate_tokens()

Examples

# harnessr ships no prices, so a built-in model's cost is NA until you set
# them. Not 0: nothing says the run is free.
hr_estimate_cost("gpt-4o", input_tokens = 120000, output_tokens = 4000)
#> [1] NA

# Set the prices you pay. These figures are illustrative: use your
# provider's current prices, in USD per million tokens.
hr_register_model("gpt-4o", input_usd = 2.50, output_usd = 10)
hr_estimate_cost("gpt-4o", input_tokens = 120000, output_tokens = 4000)
#> [1] 0.34

# Where the figure's prices came from.
hr_estimate_cost("gpt-4o", 120000, 4000, detail = TRUE)
#>    model  usd priced   as_of certain
#> 1 gpt-4o 0.34   TRUE 2026-11    TRUE
